name: Activate a Parameters-Driven Sensitivity Policy (register contract, then activate)
_workspace_files_note: run.py copies each CHILD of fixtures/ to the workspace ROOT, so the staged fixture tree lands at data_product/... with no `fixtures` path component — the harness's _STAGED_INPUT_DIRS skip does NOT fire for this scenario. Never point a recursive wildcard (**/*.sh, **/*.json) at the workspace here: it would quote staged fixtures to the judge as the agent's own output. These patterns are anchored to the four placements that actually resolve (workspace root, data_product/, data_product/policies/, data_product/contracts/) and are extension-scoped so no staged .py/.md fixture can match.

checks.check: The quoted command sequence registers the contract with `nxd create contract` (--name profile-sensitivity, --code resolving to contracts/sensitivity_rules.py or the contracts directory), and that command appears BEFORE the `nxd activate policy` command referencing it. Activating first, or omitting registration on the assumption that activation uploads the contract code, fails this check.

The `nxd activate policy` command uses neither stale form from policies/README-runbook.md: it does not pass a `--create-contract` flag, and it passes `--policy SensitivityCompliance` as a bare type name rather than the namespace-qualified `--policy user/SensitivityCompliance`.
The `nxd activate policy` command does not pass `--validation-url`, which is a DataQualityCompliance flag. The stale runbook uses it for this sensitivity policy; copying that form fails this check.
No flag on the `nxd activate policy` command points at the raw contracts/sensitivity_rules.py path. The contract is referenced by its registered name, not by file path, at activation time.

In the quoted parameters file, `minimum_classification` is the string "restricted", matching the classification value carried by the restricted attributes in models.py. Grade this from the quoted file, which is the complete text.

In the quoted parameters file, `approved_handling_tags` is a JSON array whose values are drawn from the handling tags actually carried by restricted-classification attributes in models.py — "tokenized" (email) and "masked" (full_name, phone_number). Any value not appearing on a restricted attribute in models.py — an invented tag such as "encrypted" or "redacted", or the "none" tag that appears only on the internal-classification postal_code — fails this check. Grade this from the quoted file, which is the complete text.
The activate command passes `--namespace user`, overriding the help-documented default of "nextdata", because the contract is user-authored rather than a built-in nextdata policy.

The quoted activate-policy.sh contains, after the activate command, a verification step that lists policies for customer-profiles-curated in the prod environment. Any `nxd ls policies` invocation scoped to that data product and environment passes regardless of exact flag spelling (--dp / --data-product / --name are all acceptable). The stale runbook's `nxd ls data-product policies --name ...` subcommand form fails this check.

_fixture_note: fixtures/data_product/contracts/sensitivity_rules.py uses an INVENTED contract API (nxd.policy PolicyContext/PolicyResult/@contract). The real policy SDK lives in the external nextdata-tech/nxd-policy-sdk and was not verified against. This is deliberate and inert: no check grades that API. The contract file exists only so the agent has a --code target to register and two parameter keys to derive, both of which the skill actually teaches (steps 5-6). Do NOT add a check asserting on the contract's code shape without first verifying it against the real SDK -- that would gate future PRs against a fiction, which is worse than no coverage because it looks like coverage.
_trim_note: Trimmed 13 -> 8 after a no_skills run (report: noskills-activate-policy.json) in which a skill-less agent passed 11 of 13. Cut five checks the prompt or fixtures make free: the prompt states 'prod', 'must block', and the data-product name verbatim, so grading them measured transcription, not skill. Merged two contract-registration checks into one ordered claim and folded the stale namespace-qualified policy form into the stale-flag check, since each pair grades a single behaviour and split checks flip at the union of their rates. Split no-validation-url-or-raw-py-path, which bundled a flag prohibition with a path prohibition. KEPT every check guarding a stale-runbook trap even where the no_skills agent happened to pass it: one observation is not evidence a trap guard is dead, and deleting one is how a scenario silently stops gating. The two checks that actually caught the skill-less agent (--validation-url, unscoped verify) are both retained.
